strategy.summary: Reproduce GH#68590 in pandas: densifying a datetime64/timedelta64 SparseArray with an object or explicit numeric dtype yields a mixed-type object array (datetime.datetime or raw ints beside a pandas-boxed fill), and a nanosecond Timestamp/Timedelta fill is truncated to microseconds in _promote_for_fill. The PR's own tests in pandas/tests/arrays/sparse/test_array.py (test_to_dense_datetimelike_non_numpy_fill, test_to_dense_datetimelike_fill_other_unit) and test_indexing.py (test_take_fill_datetimelike_string) should fail on the buggy commit 14de06cf2823 and pass on the fixed revision. The build is a Cython extension, so a compiled in-tree build is required before running tests.
strategy.test_command: python -m pytest pandas/tests/arrays/sparse/test_array.py -k 'to_dense_datetimelike_non_numpy_fill or to_dense_datetimelike_fill_other_unit' pandas/tests/arrays/sparse/test_indexing.py -k take_fill_datetimelike_string -q
strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/arrays/sparse/test_array.py::test_to_dense_datetimelike_fill_other_unit (kind M8/m8, unit s/ms/us, boxed True/False) and pandas/tests/arrays/sparse/test_array.py::test_to_dense_datetimelike_non_numpy_fill (kind M8/m8, unit s/ms/us/ns, na_fill True/False) and pandas/tests/arrays/sparse/test_indexing.py::TestTakeFill::test_take_fill_datetimelike_string (unit M8[s], m8[s])
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy commit 14de06cf2823 the selected tests fail: the to_dense/np.asarray(dtype=object) or astype(object) comparisons see mixed object contents (datetime.datetime or ints beside the fill) or a ns fill truncated to us, and the fill-other-unit test reads the fill as a raw integer under an i8 cast. On the fixed revision (the commit that includes PR #68590) all selected tests pass, with the dense result being a single consistent datetime64/timedelta64-compatible type and ngaps == 1.
strategy.numerical_probe: SparseArray(np.array([1,2,3],dtype='M8[s]'), fill_value=pd.Timestamp('1970-01-01T00:00:00.000000002').as_unit('ns')) then to_dense() and np.asarray(arr, dtype='i8') compared against the dense values.
risks: Only the datetime64/timedelta64 sparse path is affected; the bug is platform-independent in logic but depends on the numpy version's casting rules (np.result_type and np.full behaviour for datetime units), so the exact buggy output depends on the numpy version installed; pin numpy to the version the PR CI used if the transition does not appear.

The README gives no version constraint for NumPy, python-dateutil, tzdata or Cython, and no era table entry exists; the chosen versions are unbounded and were not documented by the evidence, so this plan simply uses current releases compatible with the checked-out tree.

The test_take_fill_datetimelike_string test references GH#68590 but the changelog and PR diff show the take path; if the buggy revision already parses string fills for both kinds, that test may pass on buggy and would not transition, so only the other two tests are reliable discriminators.
Compiled Cython extensions must be built for the checked-out revision; a stale build from a different commit will mask the transition, so rebuild after checkout.

No platform, sanitiser or threading requirement is stated in the evidence; the defect is expected to reproduce on a standard Linux x86_64 build, and the strategy has not been verified on other architectures.

oracle.reference_source: dense (non-sparse) result of the same values, via pd.array(values).astype(object) and np.asarray(values, dtype='i8')
oracle.why: Assertions use tm.assert_numpy_array_equal, which compares exact values and dtypes; no numerical tolerance applies to datetime/timedelta integer-backed data.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On 14de06cf2823 the object-dtype comparison receives an array whose stored elements are datetime.datetime or ints beside the boxed fill, so assert_numpy_array_equal against the dense object array fails; the fill-other-unit test densifies a ns or other-unit fill as a raw integer under the i8 cast, and the assertion fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the fill is normalized to a numpy scalar in the subtype's unit, the object and i8 results match the dense values exactly, and ngaps == 1 holds, so all parametrizations pass.
